query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a high-entropy alloy (HEA) reinforcement to a W-Cu composite can overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: W-Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Addition of a high-entropy alloy (HEA) reinforcement
generation.conditions: Heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components
generation.mechanism: The HEA reinforcement can improve the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite by reducing phase separation and interfacial void formation, and by promoting a more uniform distribution of W particles or ligaments within the Cu matrix.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite relative to the untreated composite
generation.baseline: Thermal conductivity of the untreated W-Cu composite
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures of the W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism by which the HEA reinforcement improves the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite is not fully understood and requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the thermal conductivity of W-Cu composites with and without HEA reinforcement under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite with HEA reinforcement is not significantly improved relative to the untreated composite, then the hypothesis is falsified.

In this study, AZ91 magnesium-alloy-based metal matrix composites (MMCs) reinforced with 10 wt% of Al0.5CoCrFeNi2 high-entropy alloy (HEA) particles and SiC particles were prepared by a spark plasma sintering (SPS) process at 300 °C. The effects of reinforcements on the microstructure and mechanical properties of AZ91-based MMCs were studied. The results showed that AZ91–HEA composite consisted of α-Mg, Mg17Al12 and FCC phases. No interfacial reaction layer was observed between HEA particles and the Mg matrix. After adding HEA into AZ91, the compressive yield strength (C.Y.S) of the AZ91–HEA composite increased by 17% without degradation of failure strain. In addition, the increment in C.Y.S brought by HEA was comparable to that contributed by commonly used SiC reinforcement (15%). A relatively low porosity in the composite and enhanced interfacial bonding between the α-Mg matrix and HEA particles make HEA a potential reinforcement material in MMCs.
